about: Design allowables for the printed mount (printed-mount [3JA], [Xtj]; used by the FEA, [tY3]). Built 4 Oct 2026 from the makers' datasheets (materials.json) and independent tests (independent.json). Every number traces to a source or to an assumption labelled 'ASSUMPTION'. MPa throughout. xy: load along the layers; z: load across the layers.

method.start: start = the lower of the maker's printed-specimen value and the independent typical value (median of independent results) for that property and direction. Where the maker publishes nothing, the independent value alone; where nothing independent exists, the maker's value times an 'unverified' factor (ASSUMPTION).
method.short_term: short_term = start x print(direction) x moisture x temperature
method.sustained_allow: stress from loads that never go away (the arm's own weight on the mount) <= short_term x creep_strength / SF_static
method.working_peak_allow: peak stress in normal use (walking peaks, the arm moving 1.5 kg at full reach, lying down) <= short_term / SF_static
method.fall_allow: one-off abuse case (a fall onto the back): peak stress <= short_term / SF_fall. Judged on short-term strength: a fall is brief, and some permanent damage is accepted so long as the arm stays attached
method.fatigue_range_allow_1e7: stress RANGE (max minus min) of the repeating walking load <= short_term x fatigue_1e7 / SF_fatigue, at the design life of 1e7 cycles. Combine a mean stress with a Goodman line as Puigoriol-Forcada 2018 did; the fraction comes from tension-tension R = 0.05 tests, which already carry a mean stress
method.E_design_long_term: stiffness to design against = E_low x temperature_E x creep_E. E_low = the lower of the maker's modulus and the LOWEST independent result (not the median), because the flex target must be met at the low end of the modulus
method.E_z_low: for unfilled PC: min(maker E_z, lowest independent E_z 1806, 0.74 x E_xy_low), 0.74 being Gomez-Gras 2021's measured Z/XY tensile-modulus ratio at +/-45 raster

tensile_xy_MPa.from: median of 62, 65, 59, 53, 62 (gomezgras_2021_pciso: X-Flat 0, X-Flat +/-45, X-Edge 0, X-Edge +/-45, X-Edge 90), 57.1 (rodrigues_2026), 68, 71 (cnck_pcblend_2021), 42.5, 55.0 (aldawood_2025 horizontal). X-Flat 90 (41) left out: a part is printed with alternating rasters, as the makers' specimens are

tensile_z_MPa.from: median of 26, 28, 30 (gomezgras Z-Flat), 35, 25, 43.4 (cnck upright: undried brass, dried steel, dried brass)

bend_xy_MPa.from: median of the six gomezgras X configurations

bend_z_MPa.from: median of the three gomezgras Z-Flat configurations

E_xy_low_MPa.from: rodrigues_2026 (lowest of 1549 to 2510 from rodrigues, gomezgras, aldawood); median 2236

independent_typical_unfilled_pc.z_over_xy_strength_observed: 0.35 to 0.61 (cnck), 0.43 (gomezgras +/-45); against makers' 0.90 (Bambu PC) and 0.78 (PolyMax PC)

print_xy.why: the project's prints: not annealed (Bambu's datasheet specimens were annealed and dried 80 C 12 h; Polymaker advises 90 C 2 h), X1 passive chamber rather than the heated chambers of the Stratasys tests, ordinary slicer settings. Along the layers the bead itself carries load, so the loss is small; Fang 2020 found chamber temperature had no significant effect along the bead. ASSUMPTION in its size, direction supported by the sources

print_z.why: across the layers the bond carries load. CNC Kitchen measured layer strength 25 MPa with a hardened steel nozzle against 43 MPa with brass, same filament and G-code (about 0.58); the X1 Carbon's stock nozzle is hardened steel. The independent median already includes the 25 MPa result, so 0.80 rather than 0.58; ASSUMPTION in size. Print PC hot (top of the maker's range) to recover some of it

moisture.why: PC is hygroscopic. Fang 2020 (JHU/NIST): filament at 0.15% water printed with 11.7% porosity and lost about 30% of its strength along the bead; dry filament printed at 0.16% porosity, close to bulk. 0.90 assumes the filament is dried to the maker's recipe and printed from a dry box (the AMS is not airtight enough for PC over a long print). If it is not dried, use 0.70 (Fang 2020). ASSUMPTION for the dried case

infill.why: these allowables hold for solid material. Design every load path solid (100% infill, or enough walls to fill the section near bolts, inserts and bending roots). Sparse infill is not credited: Akgumus 2026 measured PC at 17.5 MPa (30% grid) and 24.9 MPa (60% grid) on the nominal section, about 0.30 and 0.42 of the solid independent typical. If a region must be sparse, model only its walls and skins as load-bearing

temperature_strength.why: use up to about 40 C beside the electronics. ASSUMPTION: no printed-PC strength-versus-temperature data at 35 to 40 C was found; PC's glass transition is about 145 C and HDT 99 to 117 C (makers), Dogan 2022 saw no PC creep rupture at 40 C or even 60 C under 20 MPa for 3 h. 0.85 is a deliberately cautious allowance for amorphous PC losing yield strength as it warms

temperature_E.why: ASSUMPTION, as above: PC's modulus changes little from 23 to 40 C far below its glass transition

creep_strength.why: sustained-load limit, so the mount does not creep to rupture under the arm's permanent weight. Bulk PC ruptures in creep at 0.7 to 0.8 of yield within hours to days (Mu 2022); printed PC adds weak interfaces. ASSUMPTION: no long-term creep-rupture data for printed PC was found (Salazar Gabino 2018 is paywalled). 0.50, then the full static safety factor on top

creep_E.why: long-term modulus under the arm's weight. Covestro Makrolon 2805 (bulk PC, ISO 899-1, 23 C): creep modulus 1900 MPa at 1000 h against 2400 short-term (0.79). Extrapolating to a few years and allowing for printed interfaces: 0.70. ASSUMPTION in the extrapolation; replace with the measured stiffness of the printed mount after weeks under load ([lUO])

fatigue_1e7.why: walking flexes the mount on every step. Rodrigues 2026 (Stratasys PC, R = 0.05, 10 Hz): fatigue limit at 1e6 cycles 7% of static strength; their Basquin fit, stress range = 101.77 x N^-0.247, gives 1.9 MPa at 1e7, 3.3% of 57.1 MPa (our extrapolation, labelled). Gomez-Gras 2021 agrees in kind: flexural fatigue at 20% of static strength failed within 4e3 to 4e4 cycles in every orientation. Design life 1e7 cycles: at about 2 steps a second, 2 h of walking a day is about 1.4e4 cycles a day, so 1e7 is about two years. If the design life is set at 1e6, use 0.07 (measured run-out)

fatigue_1e6.why: Rodrigues 2026, measured: 1e6 run-outs at 7% and 5%, failures at 8% and above

unverified_strength.why: ASSUMPTION: applied to a maker's strength that no independent test checks (only CarbonX bending strength here)

unverified_E.why: ASSUMPTION: applied to CarbonX's 6980 MPa XY modulus, which nothing independent checks; short-fibre modulus depends strongly on how well the fibres line up with the load, and this project's raster will not match the maker's specimens. This is the most consequential single assumption in the file: measure it (see README) before choosing PC-CF on stiffness

pccf_z_over_xy.why: ASSUMPTION: no Z data exists for any PC-CF. Fibres lie in the layer plane and do not cross layer interfaces, so across the layers PC-CF is no better than its matrix and often worse. Bounded by unfilled PC's independent 0.35 to 0.61 and Bambu PAHT-CF's own 0.51 (second-hand). Also applied to bending across the layers

pccf_E_z.why: ASSUMPTION: across the layers PC-CF is matrix-dominated, so its Z modulus is taken as unfilled PC's low Z value

static.why: on stress, for the sustained and the normal working cases. The failure mode is the 3.7 kg arm dropping on a floor where people and a dog walk; across the layers printed PC fails brittly (1.4 to 1.7% strain, Gomez-Gras) with scatter up to 13 to 17% CoV; most of the data is from other printers and other PC grades; and the mount is a single load path. 3 rather than 2 until the printed adapter has been load-tested to its rated case ([vqz]); it may come down to 2 for a part that has passed that test

fall.why: a fall onto the back is rare and judged on short-term strength; the part may yield but must not let go of the arm

fatigue.why: on the stress range, over the fatigue fraction which is already a run-out or extrapolated life, not a mean

bambu_pc.basis: start values: strength along the layers and all Z values from the independent typical (below Bambu's 62/56 MPa); bending XY independent 76.6 (Bambu 108); bending Z independent 54.2 (Bambu 55); E_xy low 1549 independent (Bambu 2110); E_z low 0.74 x 1549 = 1146 (Bambu 1450). HDT 117 C (Bambu)

polymaker_polymax_pc.basis: start values: tensile XY Polymaker 53.44 (below the independent 60.5); tensile Z independent 29.0 (Polymaker 41.43); bending XY independent 76.6 (Polymaker 81.29); bending Z independent 54.2 (Polymaker does not publish it); E_xy low 1549 independent (Polymaker 2435); E_z low 1146 (Polymaker 2149). HDT 99 C (Polymaker)

3dxtech_carbonx_ezpc_cf.basis: start values: tensile XY independent 53.0 (remache_2026, Prusa PC-CF at 80% infill; 3DXTech 73); tensile Z ASSUMPTION 0.40 x 53.0; bending XY 3DXTech 85 x 0.80 unverified = 68.0; bending Z ASSUMPTION 0.40 x 68.0; E_xy low 3DXTech 6980 x 0.75 unverified = 5235 (ASSUMPTION); E_z ASSUMPTION 1146 as unfilled PC. Elongation 2.1% XY (3DXTech): brittle, notch-sensitive; keep fillets generous. Needs a hardened nozzle (the X1C has one)

comparison_for_the_designer.reading: For a part whose bending runs along the layers, CarbonX ezPC+CF's design modulus (3298 MPa, after a 25% unverified knock-down) is about 3.4 times unfilled PC's (976 MPa) for 13% more density. The same geometry is 3.4 times stiffer and 13% heavier; a plate thickened to the same bending stiffness (stiffness index E^(1/3)/density) is about 25% lighter in PC-CF. Its strength allowables are about the same as PC's along the layers and about a quarter lower across them, and it is brittle. Unfilled PC (either brand) is the fallback if the measured PC-CF modulus disappoints, or for a part whose load must cross layers.

caveats: Bambu PC and PolyMax PC come out the same in most rows because no independent test of either exists, so the same independent PC values govern both. They differ where their own datasheets are lower: PolyMax PC's XY tensile (53.4 MPa).

Fatigue governs. With the walking range roughly equal to the static stress from the arm (vertical acceleration about 0.5 g either way, an ASSUMPTION until the IMU log is read), the static stress from the arm must stay near 1 MPa in PC. A mount sized for the flex target will probably be this lightly stressed anyway; the FEA reports both.

The PC-CF numbers rest on three ASSUMPTIONs (unverified modulus, Z ratio, Z modulus) and on one independent strength from a different PC-CF brand at 80% infill. No creep or fatigue data for printed PC-CF; PC's factors are used.
Nothing here was measured on the project's X1. The plan in README replaces assumptions with measurements on printed coupons and the printed mount.
